hook_text: Slit the glued edge of a cereal box and you are looking at the drawing that made it.
clip_script: Find an empty cereal box. Find the glued edge, slit it, unfold. It lies flat in one piece: four sides in a row, top flaps above, bottom flaps below, a thin tab where the glue was. That flat shape is called a development, or a net, and every box, carton and tray in the shop started exactly like it. To draw one: four rectangles in a row in the order they go round, side, end, side, end. Top and bottom stuck to a long side. Dashed lines for folds, dark lines for cuts, every size in millimetres. Then a glue tab down the last edge, flaps for the lid, corners nicked so they do not snag. Count six faces. Fold a paper copy to check. In the factory a press cuts and creases a thousand of these a minute from one printed sheet. Every box was once flat. Now you can draw the flat.
visual_style: A whiteboard cereal box unfolds like animation into its net; the net is redrawn with dashed folds and dark cuts; a glue tab and flaps appear; it refolds into the box.
pacing: Open the box, name the shape, draw it, add tabs, close it.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw the development of a box 60 by 30 by 90 mm with a glue tab.
